boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 4 features for Nevada, measured 2026-11-10. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 4 districts (every district's IoU 1.0), because Nevada's map is still the one the Legislature enacted in November 2021, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027 and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 16 counties and Carson City, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 17 features (16 counties and Carson City, a consolidated city and county), measured 2026-11-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Nevada county elects a board of county commissioners and officers such as a sheriff and a district attorney, and Carson City elects a mayor and a board of supervisors; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap nv-county-officials.
source.applies: Nevada — statewide, all 16 counties and Carson City.

layers.label: Nevada Senate District
layers.rank_note: 21 Senate districts — smaller on average than a county, each made of two Assembly districts

source.answers: The Nevada Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 21 features, measured 2026-11-10: the plan the Legislature enacted in November 2021. Layer 5, the 2024 districts, is identical (every district's IoU 1.0). Every Senate district is exactly two Assembly districts, so the two chambers are simplified as one topology and share every boundary vertex. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: nv-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Senate member list on the Legislature's own site (leg.state.nv.us): name (from the senator's own page), party, the senator's Carson City room and telephone, the chamber's mailing address for mail during session, any work telephone printed for the senator, and the senator's e-mail address.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 182 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside Nevada (439 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Nevada (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='32'. 439 features in the app's box, which reaches into the five neighbouring states, 182 of them inside Nevada and kept in the archive, measured 2026-11-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Nevada. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City
layers.rank_note: 19 incorporated cities, Carson City among them, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city containing the point, or that the point is outside every city.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 19 features for Nevada, measured 2026-11-10: 18 cities and Carson City, which the Census records with no type because the city and its county are one government. MOST OF NEVADA IS IN NO CITY (about 1% of its land is inside one), the Las Vegas Strip among it, and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every city rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Nevada's mayors and council members was read in this pass; the card names the city and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap nv-municipal-officeholders.

layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-10: 142 points in Nevada's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Nevada — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Nevada State Capitol, 101 North Carson Street, Carson City

negative_point.note: Owyhee County, Idaho, about 17 km north of the Nevada line — outside Nevada and inside permalink_gate, so the app answers a selection there and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-10: TIGERweb's state layer names Idaho here (controls: the State Capitol returns Nevada, and a point in the open Pacific returns no state), and none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it. IDAHO'S OUTLINE HAS COVERED THIS POINT SINCE THE CHANGE THAT PUBLISHED IDAHO (batch 4 of the state-level launch, written 2026-11-12), which found it inside Idaho's outline in fleet-outlines.json and no other, AND THE POINT STAYS: measured that day on a 0.05-degree grid, no ground in this app's gate lies more than 2 km from every outline in fleet-outlines.json, so there is nowhere left to move it to. It is still outside Nevada and outside every shipped boundary file, which is all the checks that boot on it or select it ask, and a selection the app makes itself never leaves; the click that had to stay here became a Idaho routing case in the same change, and the click-stays-here check went with it, the way Kentucky's and Tennessee's points stayed put once every neighbour was served.

geometry.note: The whole-Nevada outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (16 counties and Carson City).
The 16 counties and Carson City — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 4 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the 2021 map, the same map as layer 4.
The 21 Nevada Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1, the 2021 plan, simplified in one topology with the Assembly districts.
The 42 Nevada Assembly districts, TIGERweb layer 2, the 2021 plan, simplified in one topology with the Senate districts.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Nevada elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from nv/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
